title: What remains
author: Rachita Swain
text:
Of late-evening strolls
in streaks of moonlight;
between the smell emitted from your being,
and your slow caresses--
much of you was poetry regained in me,
and much of the care about the world lost.
Very little of these chapters last.
What remains,
or rather creates itself anew,
is mere prose
in strenuous tolerance
to just live on--
Like puppets of an ill-survived world.
